projectBackground.name: Fintra Payments — Ticket Triage AI
projectBackground.context: Support wants an AI triage tool. Engineering wants to ship; compliance has concerns.

manager.name: Julia Hoffmann
manager.note: AI features fail on trust, not on demos. Show me the value, the error rate and what happens when it's wrong.

assignment.title: Make the go/no-go case
assignment.brief: Compute net saving, review volume and precision, choose guardrails and write the launch recommendation.

documents.name: Volume Data
documents.note: 5,000 tickets a month; 4 minutes saved per ticket; €30 per hour.

documents.name: Confidence Policy
documents.note: 18% of tickets go to human review.

documents.name: Pilot Results
documents.note: 90 true positives and 30 false positives on urgent-ticket flagging.

tasks.title: Net Monthly Saving
tasks.prompt: 5,000 tickets x 4 minutes saved at €30/hour, less €3,500 AI cost. What is the net saving (€)?
tasks.reasoning: Net value must include run cost.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Human Review Volume
tasks.prompt: 18% of 5,000 tickets go to human review. How many tickets?
tasks.reasoning: Human review is a real cost and safety layer.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Precision
tasks.prompt: 90 true positives and 30 false positives. What is precision (%)?
tasks.reasoning: Precision shows how often a flag is right.
tasks.tip: Choose the metric to match harm.
tasks.mistake: Reporting accuracy alone hides false alarms.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: When Not to Use AI
tasks.prompt: When is AI probably the wrong tool?
options: When a simple rule handles the case reliably and errors are costly
tasks.mistake: AI for AI's sake adds risk.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Launch Guardrails
options: Clear user notice that AI is used
tasks.reasoning: Guardrails limit harm and build trust.
tasks.mistake: Full launch without a kill switch is reckless.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

tasks.title: Launch Recommendation
tasks.modelAnswer: I recommend a staged launch to 20% of tickets. The business case nets €6,500 a month after AI costs, and the urgent-ticket flag has 75% precision, which is acceptable with human review of the 18% low-confidence cases (900 tickets). Guardrails include monitoring, a kill switch and customer notice. We will expand if precision stays above 75% for four weeks and complaints don't rise.
tasks.reasoning: A good recommendation quantifies value, risk and gates expansion on evidence.
tasks.mistake: A launch without exit criteria isn't a plan.
tasks.recommendation: Write down your reasoning and the evidence behind it so a reviewer can verify your conclusion quickly.

caseStudy.title: Case Study: The AI That Lied Politely
caseStudy.background: A bank launched an AI assistant that confidently gave wrong fee information. Complaints rose and the feature was withdrawn after three weeks.
caseStudy.challenges: No accuracy gate or human fallback.
caseStudy.solution: Nimbus requires accuracy gates, fallback and monitoring for every AI feature.

prompts: Which metric would you set as the launch gate?
How do you explain AI limits to users?
When would you kill the feature?
